spec: SESB eTender — Supplier View Dashboard ("My Bid")
purpose: A build specification for the supplier-facing dashboard, extracted from a working Flutter implementation. Hand this to an agent or developer to rebuild the same screen in another codebase. Every value here is taken from the running implementation, not invented.

dataSourceRule.statement: BUILD THIS AGAINST THE SYSTEM'S EXISTING DATA. Do not invent sample records, do not seed a fixture file, and do not hard-code the numbers shown on the tiles.
dataSourceRule.why: Every figure on this page is a count of supplier participation rows that the system already holds and already serves to another screen. Inventing a parallel dataset produces a dashboard that disagrees with the report it is meant to summarise, and the disagreement will not show up until someone compares them.

theOneSource.returns: One row per tender the signed-in supplier took part in.
theOneSource.contract: See data.record.fields for the full field list.
theOneSource.everyFigureOnThisPage: Derived from these rows by counting them. There is no second source and no computed total that is sent rather than counted.

dataSourceRule.derivedNotStored: The supplier's own name and the categories they bid in are read off their rows, not from a stored profile object. The reference implementation used to take them from a profile fixture that also carried an invented performance score; that fixture has been deleted. If your system has a real supplier profile service, read the name from it — but do not create one just to feed this page.
dataSourceRule.theOnlyExternalInput: Which supplier is signed in. That is a property of the session, not of the data, and in production it comes from the auth token — at which point the endpoint scopes its rows server-side and the client no longer needs it at all.
dataSourceRule.ifTheDataIsNotThereYet: Build against the endpoint and let the page render empty: every tile shows a muted 0, which is a truthful empty state. That is strictly better than mock rows, which make a broken wiring look like a working screen.

theme.note: Resolved hex values. The source maps these through AppColors and KPI-card constants so the dashboard and the report screens cannot drift apart; if you are porting into a system that already has tokens, map onto yours rather than hard-coding these.

tints.note: Each accent pairs with a fixed pale tint rather than an alpha blend of itself, so tinted surfaces stay consistent. Tile backgrounds additionally apply 45% opacity to the tint.
tints.muted: #F1F5F9 — muted has no tint of its own and falls back to the grey one

source.note: The same dataset the 'My Participation' report reads. This dashboard is a summary of it, so the two must never be fed from different places.

record.description: One row per tender the signed-in supplier took part in. The full contract is listed because you should bind the real record type, not a three-field subset of it — but only the fields marked usedByThisPage are read here.

fields.supplierName: string — the supplier's own name; the badge reads it from the first row
fields.supplierId: string — the supplier this row belongs to
fields.title: string
fields.tenderCategory: string — the badge's category pills are the distinct values across the supplier's rows
fields.status: string — one of statusVocabulary.values; drives every tile count
fields.paymentDate: date|null — null until the document fee is settled
fields.closingDate: date|null — the period filter tests this

doNotDisplay: bidAmount — this dashboard counts states, never values

session.signedInSupplierId: string — from the auth token in production. The only input to this page that is not a record field.

statusVocabulary.note: Wire strings exactly as the API sends them. Model these as an enum, not bare strings, so a rename is a compile error rather than a counter that silently reads zero. Parse through a fromWire() that returns null for an unrecognised value.
statusVocabulary.unknownValue: Render as itself rather than hiding the row. An unrecognised status is a finding, not a blank.

tabStrip.reason: This page has one view. A strip holding a single tab that cannot be changed is decoration, and it repeated the page heading directly beneath it. Add a strip only if a second tab exists.

sections.description: Who the signed-in supplier is, derived entirely from their own rows.

content.line1: supplierName — badgeName style, single line, ellipsised
content.trailing: One pill per derived category, accent coloured, wrapping, 6px spacing

derivation.categories: distinct non-empty tenderCategory across the supplier's rows
derivation.note: Derived from every row the supplier has, not from the rows left after the period filter: who they are does not change when they pick a shorter window.

sections.emptyCase: A supplier with no rows at all shows an empty name. Render the badge anyway — the supplier ID still identifies them.

sections.description: How far back the page is looking. A segmented control on the left, the resolved month on the right.

control.overflow: Scrolls horizontally when the row is too narrow; never wraps.

sections.rightSide: Calendar icon 16px muted, then 'Showing {MonthName} {Year}' at footnote size.
sections.wrapBehaviour: The two halves sit at opposite ends of the row and wrap onto separate lines when narrow (runSpacing 10).

sections.description: Page title on the left; what needs doing and the data vintage on the right.

right.reason: Its presence is the signal. Showing '0 responses need your action' would be noise.
right.text: '{n} responses need your action', singular '1 response needs your action'

right.note: The reference implementation says 'Prototype data as of …' because it runs on a stand-in dataset. Once the page is reading the live endpoint, either drop this line or have it state when the data was actually fetched. Do not leave the word 'Prototype' on a screen showing real figures.

sections.description: The four stages a participation request moves through, as equal cards. This is the substance of the page.

stages.note: Numbered because the numbering is the point: it tells a supplier what comes next, which a flat row of counters would not. Each tile's hint states the action the count implies, not a description of the status — a supplier reading '3 Pending Payment' needs to be told to go and pay.

unmappedStatus.note: In the vocabulary but shown on no tile: it means the tender exists, not that the supplier has done anything. Counted nowhere on this page.

header.title: stageTitle style, single line, ellipsised
header.rule: 12px gap, 1px divider in border colour, 12px gap, then the tiles

statTile.background: 45% opacity of the status colour's tint

row1.value: tileValue style; status colour normally, muted when the count is 0

statTile.label: tileLabel style
statTile.zeroHandling: A zero is greyed, never hidden. 'Nothing pending payment' is worth seeing, and a tile that disappeared would shift the ones beside it.

layout.principle: Every card the same size and every tile the same size. Those cannot both hold while a card stretches to fit whatever it contains, because stage 1 holds three tiles and the others hold two — so the tiles-per-line is decided once for the page and handed down to every card.

stagesPerRow.accept: the first count whose resulting tile width is >= minTileWidth
stagesPerRow.cards: equal width, filled by flex — never sized to their contents

tilesPerLine.fallbackWhen: no stages-per-row choice yields a tile >= minTileWidth
tilesPerLine.reason: At two abreast a three-tile stage reads as two-then-one and a two-tile stage fills its line exactly. Three abreast would leave an empty slot inside every two-tile card.

rules.rowHeights: Cards in the same row stretch to the tallest. Stage 1 carries an extra tile line, so in the 2-across layout its row is taller than the row below — inherent to wrapping.
rules.noHorizontalScroll: The stage grid must never scroll sideways. Scrolling right to read a four-step summary was the original fault; it wraps instead.

pitfalls: If the card draws a 1px border, that border comes out of the card's own width. Omitting it from the tile-width arithmetic overflows every card by exactly 2px.
Do not derive the layout from pixel breakpoints AND a minimum tile width at once. They are two ways of saying the same thing, and when they disagree the page stacks at widths that had room to spare.
Do not let each card stretch to fit its tile count. That is what made stage 1 47% wider than its neighbours.

recordScoping.rule: Show only records whose supplierId equals the signed-in supplier's.
recordScoping.warning: SECURITY — in the reference implementation this filter runs in the widget, which is a stand-in only. The endpoint must scope to the authenticated supplier server-side. A supplier must never receive another supplier's rows, because the payload would carry competitors' participation and fees even if the UI hid them.

periodFilter.window: start = first day of (currentMonth - periodMonths + 1); end = first day of next month
periodFilter.appliesTo: every tile count on the page

behaviour.counting: For each tile, count the filtered records whose parsed status equals that tile's status. A record with an unrecognised status is counted on no tile.

actionCount.definition: Sum of the counts for: Request Approved, Request Rejected, Pending Payment, Participated, Draft
actionCount.meaning: The statuses where the next move is the supplier's.
actionCount.drives: The action badge in the page header.

interactions.periodSelector: Changes the window and recounts. The only interactive control on the page.
interactions.tiles: Not interactive in the reference implementation. If you make them clickable, a tile should filter a list of the matching tenders — do not navigate away from the dashboard.

behaviour.emptyState: No special empty state. Every tile shows 0 in muted grey, which tells a supplier with no activity exactly as much as a message would.

acceptanceCriteria: All four stage cards render at the same width at every page width.
All nine tiles render at the same width at every page width.
A three-tile stage wraps as [2, 1]; a two-tile stage stays [2].
The stage grid never produces a horizontal scrollbar.
The page heading appears exactly once.
A count of zero renders as a muted 0, not a hidden tile.
Changing the period re-counts every tile without re-fetching.
Every tile count traces to rows from GET /reports/supplier-participation; nothing on the page is hard-coded or seeded.
doNotBuild: A fixture, seed file or hard-coded array of sample participation rows. Read the endpoint.
A supplier profile object invented to feed the badge — the name and categories are already on the records.
Any figure that is sent rather than counted. Every number here is a count of rows you already have.
A tab strip with a single tab.
Any figure belonging to another supplier — totals across suppliers, rankings, or counts of who else bid.
A bid amount or price anywhere on this page. The dashboard counts states, never values.
